title: Deep snow had a positive link to recorded bird richness in three of four North American feeder samples in 2001-2005 and 2021-2024
abstract: We tested the link between deep snow and recorded bird richness at feeding sites. We used 126,232 checklists from selected site-winters in eastern and western North America in 2001-2005 and 2021-2024. Each site-winter had at least two reports of no snow and two reports of more than 15 cm of snow. Models removed site-winter and state or province by year-week effects. They controlled reported effort. The four-test intervals were above zero in 3 samples and below zero in 0 samples. The estimates describe recorded species at feeders. Temperature, feeder changes, observer changes and detection can affect the results. This study does not measure population gain, pollution effects or a cause of climate change.

display.caption: Deep snow minus no snow in four selected feeder samples. Models remove site-winter and regional week effects and control reported effort. Intervals adjust for four tests.
